name: Water pump MOSFET module (D4184)
description: Opto-isolated low-side MOSFET switch for DC loads such as a 12 V water pump, solenoid valve, fan or LED strip: a PC817 optocoupler (1 kΩ series resistor) drives an AOD4184A-type 40 V N-channel MOSFET (7.6 mΩ typ at VGS 4.5 V) whose gate is biased to half the load supply and clamped by a Zener. Control input 2.5–20 V, active high, so 3.3 V and 5 V GPIOs both work; load supply 6–36 V DC, about 10 A continuous at 12 V. No flyback diode on the board. Sold as: D4184 MOSFET control module (black 35 x 16 mm board, e.g. ProtoSupplies MOD-126; 2-pin signal header PWM, GND; 3-pin load terminal +, LOAD, -).
eli5: An electronic switch for a pump: your board's tiny signal turns on a big 12 V supply to the pump, without the two ever touching.

pins.name: PWM
pins.description: Control input, active high (2.5–20 V): high = MOSFET on = load runs, low or unconnected = off. Feeds the PC817 LED through 1 kΩ, so it draws only about 2 mA from a 3.3 V GPIO. Can take PWM (keep it slow, about 1 kHz or less: the optocoupler is slow).

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Signal ground, to the microcontroller's GND. Isolated from the load side '-' on this module.
Load supply + (screw terminal), 6–36 V DC from a separate supply, not the microcontroller. The load's + lead also goes here.

pins.name: LOAD
pins.description: Load - lead (screw terminal): the MOSFET drain, pulled to '-' when the module is on. Put a flyback diode across the pump/solenoid (stripe towards +).
Load supply - / ground (screw terminal, MOSFET source). Not connected to the signal GND on the module.

supplierQuery: D4184 MOSFET control module optocoupler PWM 400W
buildNotes: Two separate circuits: PWM and GND go to the microcontroller (GPIO and GND); +, LOAD and - go to the pump and its own 6–36 V supply. Pump + lead and supply + both on '+', pump - lead on LOAD, supply - on '-'.

The load supply must be at least 6 V (9 V or more for loads over a few amps): the gate is biased to half the supply, and the MOSFET's threshold is up to 2.6 V. A 3–5 V USB mini pump powered from 5 V will not switch reliably with this module; use a 12 V pump or a logic-level MOSFET driven directly.
There is no flyback diode on the board. A pump, solenoid valve or motor is inductive: fit a diode (e.g. 1N4007 or 1N5819) across the load, stripe to '+', or the voltage spike can destroy the MOSFET.
The input is opto-isolated (PC817, 1 kΩ series resistor): about 2 mA from a 3.3 V pin, 4 mA from 5 V. Signal GND and load '-' are not joined on the board; you may leave them separate.
About 10 A continuous at 12 V with no heatsink; the D4184 gets hot above that. Small 12 V pumps (0.2–1 A) barely warm it.
PWM speed control works, but the PC817 and the 4.7 kΩ gate resistors make switching slow: keep the PWM frequency low (about 1 kHz or less) to avoid heating the MOSFET.
The on-board LED lights when the MOSFET is on (and the load supply is connected).
Never run a pump dry for long, and keep the electronics above the water line.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

pump = Pin({PWM}, Pin.OUT, value=0)  # PWM high = MOSFET on = pump runs
while True:
    pump.value(1)
    print('PUMP ON')
    time.sleep(2)
    pump.value(0)
    print('PUMP OFF')
    time.sleep(2)

test.title: The pump switches on, then off again
